question: For years, the Republic of Cyprus has continued to face serious issues of incorrect implementation of Directive 93/13/EEC on unfair terms in consumer contracts, in particular in relation to banking contracts and the effective protection of borrowers.

Recently, the Cyprus’s House of Representatives adopted legislation aimed at bringing national law in line with the requirements of this directive, and in particular the right of access to justice, with the aim of suspending foreclosures until a case is heard when unfair terms are alleged or the outstanding amount is contested.

However, the President of the Republic of Cyprus has referred this legislation back to the legislature, creating further uncertainty as to the country’s compliance with the EU acquis and effective consumer protection. In light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What does the fact that this legislation was referred back to the legislature and its nonimplementation mean for Cyprus’ compliance with EU law?
What will be the consequences of continued non-alignment with European legislation and insufficient consumer protection?
answer: Council Directive 93/13/EEC (1) requires Member States to ensure that consumers are not bound by unfair contract terms, including in mortgage contracts. However, procedures applicable to enforcement procedures must be set out in national legislation (2).

It is the primary responsibility of the national authorities and courts to ensure the monitoring and enforcement of the application of consumer law in individual disputes and to provide redress where appropriate (3).

The Commission opened an infringement procedure against Cyprus (4) concerning the correct application and enforcement of Directive 93/13/EEC and Directive 2005/29/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (5).

Further to changes of the Cypriot legislation in 2021 and 2022 (6), as well as additional data from Cyprus in 2025 on the practice of the consumer protection authorities, the Commission is finalising its assessment of the case to consider next steps. The Commission continues monitoring the situation and may decide to take further action if necessary.

Directive (EU) 2021/2167 of the European Parliament and of the Council (7), which regulates credit servicers and credit purchasers, has reinforced borrower protection, in particular by introducing general principles for the conduct of credit servicers and by establishing transparency obligations towards borrowers. Cyprus notified complete transposition of Directive (EU) 2021/2167 on 12 November 2024.
The Commission has opened an informal dialogue with Cyprus to seek clarifications on various issues arising from the national transposition.
